lxc_8c33e74dc78b6b7f.text: A French worker must get a break after 6 hours, many Americans buy food without leaving their car, and Japanese workers have carried packed lunches for about 300 years.

lxc_45396f3f539ce0bd.text: Each habit comes from real conditions such as laws, distances, workdays and the land.

lxc_4dc6ebc622ecaeb8.text: Imagine it is 12:30 in a French office.

lxc_3ee48abf3c112f85.text: People stand up, close their computers and leave their desks.

lxc_8bce79087dccd85e.text: A visitor might think, "The French just love to relax."

lxc_ebe430eda7d12c46.text: But much of this comes from rules.

lxc_1ff5ce6847fa77c6.text: In France, a full-time work week is 35 hours.

lxc_4138eb76a28043e9.text: If people work more, the extra hours count as overtime.

lxc_a96d2640486ee6b6.text: There is also a rule about breaks.

lxc_0b4f0c58569b9141.text: After 6 hours of work in a row, a worker must get a break of at least 20 minutes.

lxc_9b56063b685fe544.text: In practice, lunch is often longer, around 45 minutes.

lxc_cf42d9790fa69349.text: This time is usually unpaid, because the boss does not direct workers during lunch.

lxc_39566aa4994fab67.text: So the lunch break really belongs to the worker.

lxc_e19c0d9d8cd6a3ac.text: If a company has 50 or more workers, it must give them a room for eating.

lxc_cf32ac195af9119e.text: The room needs places to keep and heat food, and seats.

lxc_fa3e91d449283a36.text: A typical French breakfast is quick: bread with butter or jam, and a café au lait.

lxc_0f22ad6de352b7a3.text: So the day has a fast start and a protected middle.

lxc_fc3c89dc0e38adb9.text: But the French day is not always short.

lxc_e6ad21da3830103c.text: The usual limit is 10 hours of work in one day.

lxc_fd7e4735f38437c7.text: In special cases, such as a very busy period, it can go up to 12 hours.

lxc_a102957a2b40884a.text: So the 35-hour week is a starting point, not a promise of easy days.

lxc_8eb400c6c0f0a141.text: Fast food and American eating habits put pressure on French food, especially for young people.

lxc_590060e418ec208b.text: Many French people still protect their food traditions through education and laws.

lxc_1a82f9996bbe8a88.text: Now imagine a morning in an American town.

lxc_17dcccf04f523ff3.text: A woman gets into her car.

lxc_5d7ec6a51f622243.text: She drives to work, stops at a window, orders coffee and food, and keeps driving.

lxc_3ea628467663bc4f.text: This habit did not appear by chance.

lxc_1377d00fc643fb85.text: In the United States, many people use cars every day.

lxc_c8f38c5eb03dd23c.text: Because so many people drove, drive-in and drive-through restaurants became popular.

lxc_0531e4d970be1f93.text: These restaurants changed daily eating habits.

lxc_4fb5e1208832d8c8.text: In 2014, the average American adult took 26.8 minutes to travel to work.

lxc_b2bda595caa58b28.text: That is a lot of time inside a car, and food fits easily into that time.

lxc_6c4e2de4ade2953c.text: Today, American food culture gives a big place to fast food and take-out meals.

lxc_81b0c0b01ce3c47b.text: These meals come from many different cultures.

lxc_68befd667de9179d.text: Think of burgers, pizza, hot dogs, fried food, milkshakes, barbecue and Tex-Mex dishes.

lxc_cd9e0cf85f26062f.text: Many of these foods are easy to eat with your hands, even in a car.

lxc_f71891ea4879ae68.text: So the drive-through is not only about Americans "loving to hurry".

lxc_51452d535409c075.text: It is a smart answer to a simple fact: many people spend their day moving by car.

lxc_36f92dd728b3d589.text: If people come by car, the restaurant comes to the car window.

lxc_01cae209f2ecdce6.text: In Japan, many people take a different path.

lxc_dcccb4053472668f.text: In Tokyo, people usually travel to work by train, not by car.

lxc_d032d3a6647f8962.text: At lunch, someone may open a small box.

lxc_ededa0f8943b06cc.text: Inside, there are several sections: rice, some fish or meat, and vegetables.

lxc_66aeb19e87abc4fe.text: A bento is a packed meal for one person, usually for lunch.

lxc_d3bc875794185e07.text: It often has rice or noodles, fish or meat, and pickled or cooked vegetables.

lxc_601085e27fe74c11.text: It looks like a small version of a traditional Japanese meal.

lxc_39473bfeb9952174.text: That meal centers on rice and miso soup, with fish, pickled vegetables and cooked vegetables.

lxc_47d1843177b11564.text: These meals also follow the seasons.

lxc_dad0a545808e1e27.text: Why did people start carrying lunch?

lxc_3d343cfc0061da6f.text: Long ago, lunch was not a normal meal in Japan.

lxc_4dee11b6eca36937.text: It became common only in the early 18th century.

lxc_38c5ab7391aa0f0a.text: Kerosene lamps let people stay awake and active for longer.

lxc_7fadebd69d2a6337.text: Days grew longer, so people needed food in the middle.

lxc_42905fe698340045.text: Workers started bringing bentos to work.

lxc_fbf9239b83f57a28.text: They worked far from home, so their food had to stay good when cold.

lxc_2c06291fa1a0ea70.text: They used wooden boxes called menpa.

lxc_4ca9a8653012caf0.text: They filled them with barley rice and pickled plums.

lxc_d150b43bc08f149c.text: The wood kept the food fresh, even when it was cold.

lxc_6a15eeb1fc0f8f78.text: On very long days, like rice-planting days, villagers shared large wooden buckets of rice balls and side dishes.

lxc_1fb5cacdbc1d4ab9.text: Bentos were also part of fun, not only work.

lxc_7dcd541f8f6f1d97.text: Makunouchi bentos were served during breaks at the theater.

lxc_ec153e6496e8d270.text: They had grilled rice balls, fish cakes and simmered dishes.

lxc_da799009c8e17664.text: This style is still common today.

lxc_49da9c6505b9bf88.text: So the bento is not just about being neat.

lxc_18c3fe0f12833476.text: It grew from longer days, distance from home and food that works cold.

lxc_1000a307e6dacfe3.text: The land also changes what goes on the plate.

lxc_b94fcc1399e443b3.text: Japan is a group of islands, and the sea is close to many people.

lxc_00852e2979072900.text: This is why seafood is so important in Japanese food.

lxc_66eb27fa973799e8.text: Fish in a bento is not an accident.

lxc_a260045182720b7e.text: It reflects the sea around the country.

lxc_c434894f67de8fd4.text: The United States is very large.

lxc_4805a0f30513be05.text: Because of this size, food and eating habits change from region to region.

lxc_6fce5eaa354abcc9.text: American food also grew more varied in the 20th century.

lxc_62abb23ebeb91f3c.text: Technology, wars, science and immigration all played a part.

lxc_89a049af177a4b5c.text: So "American food" is really many foods, not one.

lxc_609cbf4048f090eb.text: France shows the limits of this idea.

lxc_e73a16c72e763f8d.text: French food has a long history, going back to the 14th century.

lxc_192697042ceb0aaf.text: Cheese and wine are big parts of it.

lxc_9efc57925bdfda96.text: The French place great value on enjoying food.

lxc_d42a0b79cdfb348d.text: Here, tradition, education and laws shape food as much as the land does.

lxc_5721ffd7ee46e9d7.text: Even the lunch break comes from work rules, not from mountains or seas.

lxc_88473b3bb40eb6c4.text: So geography is a strong force, but it is one force among several.

lxc_c2c96cfbe5d1bb9d.text: Laws, cars, lamps, distance and history all have a part.
